prerequisites: Successful completion of the modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.
Recommended: Lectures Materials Science 1 and 2 for the 'Structure of Technical Materials' course.

learning_outcomes.text: Derive the structure of technical, metallic materials based on the fundamental properties of crystalline solids.
Understand the mechanisms that lead to particularly high material strengths, especially heat treatment processes.
Assess the potential and limits for the use of extremely stressed materials based on knowledge of relevant physical phenomena.
Acquire the foundations for the new or further development of materials or the possibilities for adaptation to special load collectives.
Learn common methods of systematic material selection.
Apply material selection methods to a specific application case.
Identify material classes and select the most suitable material using material characteristic values and selection charts.
Develop a better understanding of the presented material classes.
Recognize in which specific application case the individual material classes provide an effective advantage.

syllabus_topics: Holistic consideration of requirements for a material system
Required fundamentals of materials science
Methodological competencies in systematic material selection
Interfaces of material selection in the development process
Derivation of material characteristic values and material property diagrams for the development process
Technical implementation using practical examples in the fields of: Classic metallic lightweight materials
Technical implementation using practical examples in the fields of: Fiber-reinforced plastic composites
Technical implementation using practical examples in the fields of: Hybrid material systems
Consideration of further requirement profiles such as manufacturing, costs, recycling, EcoAudit
Extension of technical implementation based on additional factors and their evaluation
Consequences of incorrect material selection
Steel grades
High-strength materials: martensitic hardening steels (Maraging Steels)
High-strength materials: manganese hard steels / metastable austenitic steels
High-strength aluminum alloys
Titanium alloys
High-temperature materials: near α-titanium alloys
High-temperature materials: ferritic chromium steels
High-temperature materials: austenitic steels
High-temperature materials: nickel-based superalloys
High-temperature materials: high-temperature ceramics
High-temperature materials: thermal barrier coatings
assessment_rules: The module examination can be a written exam (180-240 minutes) or an oral exam (45-60 minutes). In the exam, students should explain underlying methods for exemplary problem statements and find detailed solutions for calculation examples. Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
